text: In spite of these conciliatory proposals, General Yang Sen remained expenditure, and his attitude stiflered to one of deliance. He was only after all attempts at an unicable settlement had failed, and in view of the dangerous and humilining position of "the two British steamers and the mayole" vessel, Cookehaer, that the British shallow delight gunboat. Widgeon and the merchant steamer Kiwa, married by a zenvil detachment which had been ordered to proceed from lehang to Wanhsen, were authorised to use force as a last resource.

label: text

Franklin, August 21.
The Japanese xunbaht "Sundida" was fired upon by sentinels of the southern troops at 9 a.m. yesterday at a point 30 miles up the Yangtze River from Yochow, while going up the river from Hankow to Linginai to protect the navigation of steamers. Ego bullets took effect in the sailors' quarters, but Fortunately there were no casualties. Rear Admiral Nagano, the Commander-in-Chief, has filed a strong protection with General Thong Samrchi against the violent action on the part of the Chinese soldiers,... Shipping & Engineering.

label: paragraph_title
text: EARLIER REPORT

label: text
text: Following Yang Sen's seizure of the two Butterfield & Swire's steamers; Yang Sen refused to talk with the commander of H.M.S. Cockchafer, which was lying at Wan Hsien and insisted on discussing the matter with the Consul, who accordingly "proceeded to Wan Hsien from Chungking.

label: text
text: The Consul demanded the removal of the Chinese guards from the captive steamers as a preliminary measure, but met with a stubborn refusal, although he offered to guarantee that the offending vessel should return to Wan Hsien or that the other two steamers should remain until the matter of the sinking of the two junks was settled.

label: text
text: H.M.S. Widgeon was then ordered to proceed to Wan Hsien and also the steamer Kiawo, carrying a party of marines, as a display was thought advisable in view of the Chinese attitude.

label: text
text: On Sunday evening H.M.S. Widgeon and the Kiawo, accompanied by H.M.S. Cockchafer, entered Wan Hsien harbour when they were heavily fired on with guns and rifles from Wan Hsien.

label: text
text: As their position became immediately very dangerous 'the gunboats returned fire, while retiring down-stream to Ichang.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: RAILWAY PERILS.

label: paragraph_title
text: THREE FRESH ACCIDENTS REPORTED.

label: text
text: London, September 7.

label: text
text: An express travelling to London from Glasgow over-ran the buffers at Leeds station "early this morning. The engine crashed through two walls and demolished the end of the station, stopping within a few feet outside a cab rank opposite. The hotel roof at the station end fell on the engine. There were no casualties.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: Chicago, September

label: text
text: Eight persons were killed and over a hundred injured in a collision at Courtlan Street Station between two passenger trains. Two wooden cars at the rear of a stationary train, containing holiday makers, were telescoped.—Reuter.

label: text
text:
Vancouver, September 7.
Four persons were killed when a goods train jumped the rails of a bridge a hundred miles east of here. Fire broke out destroying the bridge. Twenty-six cars were partially burnt and precipitated into a canyon a hundred feet below.—Router.

label: paragraph_title
text: ONE BIG UNION

label: text
text: LIVELY DISCUSSION AT "CONGRESS.

label: text
text: OVERNMENT CRITICISED.

label: text
text: A lively discussion at the Trade Union Congress centred on the resolution of the General Workers' Union demanding the discouragement of the formation of new organisations with "One Big Union" as their ultimate goal.

label: text
text: The Congress finally adopted an agreement asking the Council to call conferences of trade groups in order to promote the merging of separate unions.

label: text
text: Thereafter an emergency resolution was carried expressing concern at the tendency of the present Government to interfere needlessly with the liberty of the subject and to utilise methods of repression in industrial disputes, and protesting against the unwavering application of emergency powers notwithstanding "the peaceful atmosphere of the mining dispute."

label: text
text: The proposal of the General Council to impose a penny levy per member for the next three years in connection with the Easton Lodge labour education scheme, for which £50,000 is required for alterations and developments, was rejected by 2,441,000 votes against 1,481,000. Countess Warwick had donated Easton Lodge for labour education. Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: TRAIN OUTRAGE

label: paragraph_title
text: CONFESSION BY TWO CRIMENALS.

label: text
text: HORRIFIED BY SPECFACE

label: text
text: Amested in a casual ward a musician named Otto Salesinger (21) and a merchanic, Willy Weber (22) confessed their responsibility for the railway smash at Lehrte on August 19.

label: text
text: They said that they were employed and penniless for months and decided to derail the train and rob the passengers and mail. They loosened the rails and hid in the bushes, but were so horrified at the resultant spectacle that they fled without waiting to rob.

label: text
text: The deed preyed on the mind of Weber, who confessed to his brother at his father's grave, after which the Police got on the trail.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: MILLION AND A HALF ON THE LIST.

label: text
text:
Rugby, September 7.
The Ministry of Labour announces that on August 30, the total number of persons recorded unemployed in Great Britain was 1,549,800. This was 9,198 less than a week ago, but 1,954,08 more than a year ago.

label: text
text: It is exclusive of the persons who have ceased work in the coal mixing industry on account of the dispute.—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: A LEGAL POINT.

label: paragraph_title
text: CLOSED RESTAURANTS AND COURTS.

label: paragraph_title
text: MR. LO'S ARGUMENT.

label: text
text: Arguing for the defence of a Chinese restaurant keeper who was summoned before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning for keeping his premises open after regulation hours, Mr. M. W. Lo said that the condition of the licence was that the restaurant should be closed at 2 a.m., but nothing was mentioned about the door. It was necessary, he said, for the inmates to open the door in order to get some air, but so long as customers had not been served with drinks he thought no offence had been committed.

label: text
text:
To further illustrate his point, Mr. Lo said that the doors of a court house may be open, but the court will be “closed” so long as a Magistrate is not sitting there.
His Worship thought that a technical offence has been committed and imposed a fine of $10

label: paragraph_title
text: POLICE OFFICER ILL.

label: text
text: Friends of Mr. G. M. Dorrington, Sub-Inspector of Police and at present attached to the Mongkok Station, will regret to hear that he is "lying seriously ill in the Kowloon Hospital."

label: text
text: Mr. Dorrington entered hospital about four days ago suffering from a chest complaint. His condition was stated to be very serious on enquiry being made this afternoon.

label: doc_title
text: OUT WITH THE REDS!

label: text
text: A REFERENDUM PROPOSED.

label: text
text: A great crowd filled the Royal Albert Hall, Kensington, W., on July 15, at a mass meeting to protest against Soviet interference in British affairs.

label: text
text: Col. John Gretton, M.P., presided, and others on the platform included Lord Clive, Lord Struthspey. Commander O' Locker-Lampson, M.P., Mr. G. Havelock Wilson, the President of the Seamen's Union, and many Conservative M.P.'s.

label: text
text: Mr. Joseph Martin, who was blinded by the treatment he received in Russian prisons and whose case was mentioned in the House of Commons, sat behind the speakers, Commander: Oliver Locker-Lampson, M.P., who commanded armoured-car contingents in Russia during the war when that country was an Ally of Great Britain, said:

label: text
text: The Soviet owes private British creditors alone more than £250,000,000, and I ask. What right had we to recognize this swindling syndicate until it had owned up and paid up?

label: text
text: It can establish companies in Great Britain for trade, like Acros, and Arcos can issue a writ for libel, as it has done against the "Daily Mail." But no Englishman can bring any action in our Law Courts for damages for his losses in Russia.

label: text
text: Why, an Englishman can even watch wood coming into the country from Russia and he can actually identify it as his own timber because it bears his mark, but he cannot recover one rouble.

label: text
text: Petrol which is ours has been sent over and dumped below cost price upon the British market. It is disposed of by the agency known as Russian Oil Products, Limited.

label: text
text: The Government fears that a withdrawal of recognition might be treated as tantamount to a declaration of war. I should like to ask if the persistent Bolshevik meddling in our affairs is not tantamount to ten declarations of war?

label: paragraph_title
text: Diplomatic Slobber.

label: text
text: I am tired of hearing the Soviet referred to by his Majesty's Ministers as a "friendly State," and sick to death of the diplomatic Slobber with which we fawn upon these fiends. There was a ringing mandate from the constituencies at the last election to kick them out, and we should long since have swept the stable clean. But our Government does not propose to act. And yet the peril is as grave as any since the war.

label: text
text: Will the Government forthwith take a referendum in this grave emergency? If to each citizen, simply and straightly, the question "is put—Yea or Nay, under which flag will you live; the bloody banner of Bolshevism or the Union Jack? I know in advance what England's answer will be.

label: text
text: At one point in Commander Locker-Lampson's speech a well-dressed woman shouted some remarks that were inaudible. There were cries of "Up the Reds!" and counter-eries of "Put her 'out!'" Waving her arms and shouting "Up the Reds" the woman was escorted from the hall by stewards.

label: text
text: A Mountain of Murder

label: text
text: Brigndier-General Sir Henry Page Croft, M.P., proposed a resolution protesting against the activities of the Soviet agents in the Empire and supporting the Government in any steps they might take to deal with the menace. He said that in Russia anti-Christ was enthroned upon a mountain of murder.

label: text
text: I warn you that the Soviet Governments are making war on our country every day and that several great trade unions have passed, without the knowledge of their members, under the control of the Minority Movement, which is the British branch of the Red International. We feel for the miners because we see they are being used by Mr. Cook to achieve his vainglorious aims. Those people who have come to make trouble in our midst should be given 48-hours notice.

label: paragraph_title
text: TSINGTAO.

label: text
text:
LIQUOR AND BEER TAXES PAID
UNDER PROTEST.

label: text
text: TREATY RIGHTS:

label: text
text: Foreign importers, including British, Germans, Russians and Japanese, have been paying the liquor and beer tax under protest since it was put into effect on August 23, and are obtaining receipts, hoping to recover their tax payments when the impost is abolished. Representations have been made to Peking by the British, American, German and Japanese consular officials protesting against the tax which is collected by a specially organised bureau called the Kiao-no Territory, Wine, Spirit and Tobacco Tax Bureau. As no tobacco has been moved since the tax became operative no taxes have been paid on that commodity.

label: paragraph_title
text: Tsingtao, Aug. 29.

label: text
text: The method by which the authorities were able to enforce payment of the tax was to detain imports in what's godowns whither they were removed upon arrival until receipts showing that the tax had been paid to the tax office were presented.

text: Wrongful Arrests.

label: text
text: The enforced collection of such a tax is considered a further indication of the disregard of the local Chinese authorities for foreign treaty rights. This was hitherto apparent in the arbitrary arrests of

The last time he spent the night there in a cell of the type reserved for common criminals." The Japanese have found direct action effective in such cases.

label: paragraph_title
text: The Cholera Scourge.

label: text
text: Cholera has made serious inroads here and Tsingtao has been declared an infected port. Few foreigners have contracted the disease but the daily number of deaths among Chinese is from five to 30. The British Consul has warned his subjects against sea bathing, while the American squadron in port has issued orders to the officers and sailors to refrain from eating raw fruits and vegetables. The entire crew of the U.S. Seaver has been kept on that vessel for the past two days because of a case of cholera among the crew. It is learned that the sailor was almost on the point of death, but rallied and will recover.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: POKFULAM ACCIDENT.

label: text
text: An earth coolie in the employment of the Sang Fat contractors at Pokfulam Road was fatally injured in a fall from a motor lorry yesterday.

label: text
text: The vehicle was taking a sharp corner when the coolie who was seated at the back overbalanced himself and fell on the roadway, alighting on his head.

label: text
text: The accident happened at 10 o'clock yesterday morning and the injured man was immediately taken to the Government Civil Hospital, but he expired soon after admittance.

label: paragraph_title
text: THIEF'S EXCUSE.

label: text
text: SPENT ALL ON A BIT OF WOOD.

label: text
text: MAGISTRATE'S REMARK.

label: text
text: When charged before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning with unlawful possession of a piece of wood, a Chinese claimed that he paid 70 cents for it to a man with whom he struck a bargain on a vacant piece of ground.

label: text
text: In answer to a question as to how much money he had with him now, defendant said he had not a single cont.

label: text
text: His Worship: No money at all, yet you spent your last 70 cents on a piece of wood! What is the good of telling lies?

label: text
text: Defendant, who was identified as a previous offender, was sent to prison for four weeks with hard labour.

label: paragraph_title
text: A MOTHER'S WISH

label: paragraph_title
text: WANTED HER SON SENT TO PRISON.

label: text
text: A THEVING LAD

label: text
text:
For his thleving tendencies, Chinese boy had incurred the pleasure of his mother who implored the Magistrate (Major Willson) to send the boy to prison. It was stated that the lad stole a kettle from the house and handed it to another to sell it. The latter was afraid to do so, and in the end they both sat down in the street with the kettle between them, apparently in a quandary.
When the woman heard that the sentence of the court was eight strokes with a cane, she asked the magistrate to consider sending him to prison, as she thought that would be the best way to teach him a lesson. His Worship said that a beating would have a more deterrent effect than imprisonment. The woman was not convinced and had to be forcibly removed.

label: text
text: Present occupants of the Ka Chan restaurant (42 Caine Road), notified the Police that three old rifles were discovered in the premises. The arms were handed over. It is surmised that these weapons were concealed on the premises, by former tenants who took part in Kwangtung military affairs twelve years or so ago, and who have not subsequently claimed ownership, having “retired” from official life.
